fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. David says, “As for the saints in the land, they are the excellence in whom all my delight resides.” He names the saints in the land as the ones he delights in. That's a good kind of friend group.
Not this time. The kings of the nations don't show up in this verse. David says the people he delights in are “…the saints in the land…” Those are the ones he names.
Nope, no followers in this verse. David says the thing that multiplies is sorrows: “Sorrows will multiply to those who chase other gods.” No fan club, baker. Just sorrows.
Not this time, baker. The verse says, “The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup…” The portion David picks isn't a sword. It's the LORD Himself.
Good thinking, but the verse doesn't say throne. It says, “The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup…” That's the pick, friend. No cushion required.
I can see the guess, but a crown isn't what David names. The verse says, “I will bless the LORD who counsels me…” It's about advice, not a crown. Counsel is what he says the LORD gives him.

That's right, baker. David says God will not “…let Your Holy One see decay.” Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, later says David looked ahead and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ (Acts 2:31). One line in a psalm, and it points straight to the resurrection.
